# The production main.js carries the build machine's absolute file path

## Context

The engine's public production bundle includes the absolute path of the machine that built it:

```
$ curl -s https://neomjs.com/dist/production/main.js | grep -o "file:///[^\"' ]*"
file:///Users/<builder>/…/node_modules/neo.mjs/src/Main.mjs
```

The home directory and folder layout are elided here, but they are present in the published file. The `neomjs/pages` checkout's `dist/production/main.js` carries the same string. Two independent sightings:
- this measurement (2026-11-08 ~19:10Z);
- private `neo-pro` PR #58, whose production demo build sets `module.parser.javascript.importMeta: false` for one reason: keeping this path out of its own `main.js`.

Captured first as defect-note `1d3575b4`.

## The Problem

Every production build publishes the builder's file system path: a user name, a directory layout, whether the engine sat under `node_modules`. Each release cut and each pages deploy re-publishes it, with the path of whoever ran the build that time. A consuming workspace that builds for production inherits the same leak, unless it disables `import.meta` parsing wholesale, as neo-pro #58 had to.

The check behind it also stops meaning what it says. It is supposed to read where the engine *runs* from, but in a webpack build it reads where the engine was *built* from.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/Main.mjs` `importAddonModule()`, line 489: `if (isWorkspaceAddon && (Neo.config.environment !== 'dist/esm' || import.meta.url.includes('/node_modules/neo.mjs/')))`. It came in with #18712.
- **Design authority:** that method's JSDoc, quoted: "An engine running from its installed package finds them at the workspace root, three levels above its `src/`. Only an emitted `dist/esm` engine shares a tree with them, in its own `main/addon/`. `environment` alone cannot tell the two apart: a `dist/esm` config still runs from the package when its page loads the MicroLoader there." The intent is a runtime test of the page's own tree.
- Webpack 5 parses `import.meta` by default (`module.parser.javascript.importMeta: true`) and replaces `import.meta.url` with the build-time `file://` URL of the source module. The production main config, `buildScripts/webpack/production/webpack.config.main.mjs`, sets no parser option. Its output is `library: {type: 'module'}`, so a runtime `import.meta` stays valid there.
- In a `dist/production` page, `Neo.config.environment !== 'dist/esm'` is already true, so the `||` never evaluates the inlined string. Runtime behaviour is unaffected; the string only ships.
- `dist/esm` is not built by webpack, so `import.meta.url` there is the real runtime value. That is the case the check exists for.
- Line 489 is the only `import.meta.url` in `src/` (`grep -rn "import\.meta\.url" src`). In the pages tree, `main.js` is the only production file that contains `file:///`.
- The branch's unit coverage lives in `test/playwright/unit/main/MainWorkspaceAddon.spec.mjs`.

## The Fix

1. Stop webpack from inlining `import.meta.url` into `main.js`. Set `module.parser.javascript.importMeta: false` in the production main config, the one bundle that carries the path. Before widening the switch to other configs, check that no dependency's `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` asset resolution depends on it.
2. A guard on the build output: the production build, or a unit-tier check over a production build, fails when any emitted `.js` or `.mjs` file contains `file:///`. That way the next `import.meta.url` cannot reintroduce the leak quietly.

Decision Record impact: none (build hygiene inside the existing production pipeline).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npm run build-all` (production) emits no file under `dist/production` that contains `file:///`. Receipt: the grep, before and after, in the PR.
- [ ] The workspace-addon branch in `importAddonModule()` still resolves `WS/` addons in `dist/production` and `dist/esm`, and `MainWorkspaceAddon.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] A guard fails on a planted `file:///` string in a production output file, and passes on the real build.
- [ ] Post-merge: the next pages deploy serves a `main.js` without the path (`curl … | grep -c "file:///"` → 0).

## Out of Scope

- Rewriting the `WS/` addon resolution itself.
- Development mode, which serves source modules and has no bundle.
- neo-pro's own build, which follows once this lands (neo-pro #58 can then drop its workaround).

## Avoided Traps

- **Masking the symptom on the pages side** (stripping the string after the build): the bundle stays wrong for every other consumer.
- **Turning `importMeta` off without checking asset URLs**: `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` is how webpack finds some assets, so the scope is a measured choice, not a global switch.

## Related

- #18712, which introduced the check;
- private neo-pro #58 (#39), whose demo build needed the workaround;
- defect-note `1d3575b4`.

included, shipped the absolute path of the machine that built it. The

page's. The production main config now sets

runtime import.meta.url; it is an ES module, where that is valid.

check-dist-paths.mjs fails on any .js or .mjs under the build folder
that contains a file:/// URL, and build/all.mjs runs it after every
production thread build. A new import.meta.url therefore cannot ship
the path quietly. A dist build before this change fails it on main.js;
after it, the check passes.
